Hi Joan,

Are the ID and filename correctly recognized in the part2 csv report "part2_summary.csv"?

If not, what value did you use for argument 'idloc'? Probably you need to use idloc = 2 such that it uses the filename as identifier rather attempting to extract the ID from the filename.

Did you work with the data on different machines? If yes, how does it go when you process a raw file like '002492_41265.cwa' from binary all the way to part5 on a single computer?

Less likely, but an other route to investigate: The first part of the new filename (the part that is NA in your filename) is generated from the output of R command sort(dir(x)) where 'x' is the path to the directory where the "meta/ms5.out/....RData" files are stored.
What happens if you apply sort(dir(x)) to that directory path on the R command line (or also known as console window)? Do you see NA values? If yes, then maybe the directory is filled with empty filenames or somehow filenames R cannot recognize.

If this does not address it, can you create a new issue on https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues? There is a better place for discussing specific issues like yours, that do not have a quick answer.

Best, Vincent

Hi Vahan,

Part2 provides 6 estimates of MVPA, including one that looks for 10 minute bouts. By default it does this based on 5 minute epoch length.
See also variable  _MVPA_E5S_B1M80_T100  and the documentation for function g,analyse. However, you are right that the 1, 5 and 10 minute bouts lengths is all part 2 does, those bout lengths cannot be changed by the user.

I would would recommend working with part5 of GGIR which offers a lot more functionality for MVPA bout calculation.
For example, argument boutdur.mvpa of the g.part5 function allows you to specify the bout length, including the study of complementary ranges in boutl ength. For example, it can calculate time spent in bouts lasting 1-5 minutes,5-10 minutes, 10-15 minutes, and 15 minutes and over, if that is of interest to you.

Best, Vincent

As far as I know, the magnitude of the metrics provided by GGIR is not expected to be the same because of the influence of different filters to obtain them. Cut-points to classify MVPA have been proposed for ENMO, but not for the rest of the metrics, so I wouldn't expect MVPA estimates to be similar if you use different metrics and the same threshold (i.e., 100 mg by default in GGIR).

Hope this helps.

Hi,

I've gone through some previous posts where people have flagged related issues, and I saw a response back in April about a potential update to allow more than 7 days output from part 5. Our protocol involves continuous GENEActiv wear for 8 weeks.... Even for participants who wore the monitor continuously (as I can see from part 2 output), only ~7days are visible from part 5.

Is there an update on the horizon to allow analysis of long-term monitoring?

Justin
